extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers/scientists and physicians (Royal Society readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing and extracting evaluative criteria from 17th‑century Royal Society reports (anatomy, microscopy, experiments, instruments, astronomy, and clinical case histories) to judge their methodological and reporting quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of a natural history
rubrics_metrics.description: A threefold account — physiological, anatomical, and medical — taken rather from autopsy than books, and of our own country rather than the whole world; begin from the lowest degree of animation (zoophytes) and ascend by nature's clue through the several tribes, observing harmony and variety in their formation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original phrasing: "the author proposes, that there may be a threefold account given; a physiological, an anatomical, and a medical; and these taken rather from autopsy than books, and of our own country, rather than the whole world ; and to begin from the lowest degree of animation in zoophytes, or plant-animals, so ascending by nature's clue, to run through all the several tribes of animals, observing the harmony she keeps, or the liberty she takes in the various formation of them."

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize anomalous/heteroclite species
rubrics_metrics.description: Include detailed accounts of the most anomalous and heteroclite sorts of animals because one such detailed account may serve for the whole genus (example: anatomy of a porpus serving the cetaceous kind).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original phrasing: "he wishes that we had a good account of some of the most anomalous and heteroclite sorts of animals, or of those whose species are most diff'erent ; for one of these may serve in a great measure for those of the whole genus, as the anatomy of a porpus for the cetaceous kind."

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact, curious, and illustrated anatomical description
rubrics_metrics.description: Be exact and painstaking in describing each part; supply defects in prior accounts, correct errors, and illustrate the work with figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original phrasing and example: "the author has been so exact and curious in describing each part, that he has supplied several defects, and corrected many errors ... and illustrated the whole with various figures." (applied to the porpus anatomy)

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare and note affinities/differences to known species
rubrics_metrics.description: When describing anatomy or natural history, compare internal and external structures to known taxa and note affinities and differences (e.g., resemblance to dolphins and land quadrupeds, presence/absence of organs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example text: "he observes, that it is of great affinity with dolphins; that it is viviparous, lactiferous, and stands in need of respiration, like land quadrupeds ... internally it so much resembles them, that there is very little difference in the make and formation of the viscera of both; but of several parts here the structure is most remarkable."

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopy: direct, comparative, and quantitative observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use direct microscopic observation on prepared samples (e.g., fermenting wine, milk, seed), describe aggregate structures (globules, animalcules), compare across media/specimens, and report relative sizes and compositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Leuwenhoeck: "I set wine to ferment ... the lees ... made up of globules, concreted of 6 lesser ... The same also was observed in other instances ... In milk, warm from the cow, were found globules of the size only of the 6th part of a blood-globule ..." — the text shows repeated, comparative micro-observations with size references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trace development through prolonged/repeated observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow specimens across time and repeated examinations to observe development and life-cycles (e.g., tracking insect seed from non-living to living stages across months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leuwenhoeck's method: he monitored insect seed across months and reported changes — "I examined grashoppers also ... in the month of July; but, continuing my observations till the latter end of August, I found them perfectly alive ... Prosecuting my inquiry further ... I am satisfied that flies have 2 of those bladders ..."

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental reporting: document methods, materials, observations, and hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe preparation, source materials, experimental behavior under conditions, observed phenomena, and safety considerations (including variability between batches and cautions about hazardous specimens).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From phosphorus experiments: descriptions of liquid vs solid phosphorus, origin (urine or blood), behaviour when exposed to air, variability in inflammability, and explicit safety warning: "this sort is only for the experienced and careful to meddle with." Also includes specific observable phenomena (glowing, burning, fumes) and post‑experiment residues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical ophthalmic method and training for myopia
rubrics_metrics.description: Address cause of short-sightedness; use convex lenses placed between the object and eye to form an image at a comfortable distance; compensate for inverted images by inverting the text, training to read upside down, or practice viewing inverted images until accustomed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hooke's recommended expedients: (1) invert books for reading with convex lens; (2) learn to read upside down for writing; (3) train by contemplating objects inverted to gain true knowledge despite inversion. Original: "by the help of a convex glass ... the picture of the letters will appear erected ..." and suggested training approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of horizontal vane/sail design — smooth plain surface
rubrics_metrics.description: Design vanes/sails as nearly as possible to a perfect plain and smooth surface (avoid bellying or curvature) to receive maximum wind impression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original phrasing: "the vane or sail be as near as possible a perfect plain and smooth surface, without any bellying or curvity."

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of horizontal vane/sail design — allow free passages
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange vanes so the moved air has many passages between parts, preventing interception by stagnant air that would impede or divert force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original phrasing: "that the air may have as many passages between the parts of the vane or sail as may be, that the moved air may come to it as free as possible without being intercepted by a stagnant air before it, to impede or divert its force."

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of horizontal vane/sail design — middle inclination
rubrics_metrics.description: Set the plane of the vane/sail at a middle inclination between the direction of the wind and the direction of the arm (or the body of the ship) to obtain the best motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original phrasing: "that the plain of the vane or sail be put in the middle inclination, between the way of the wind and the way of the arm, or that of the body of the ship."

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomical/observational reporting: precise quantitative records
rubrics_metrics.description: Record exact timings (with corrected time), locations, altitudes, durations, and tabulate key moments (beginning, center, greatest obscuration, end) when reporting celestial events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from eclipse reports: detailed table with times for beginning, centre, greatest obscuration, end, and total duration; notes on apparent altitudes. Original entries: "Beginning of the eclipse at 1^ 50"^ 40^ in the morning, corrected time ... The whole duration 3 14 30."

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical case reporting: timeline, symptoms, interventions, diagnostic reasoning, and outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a full chronological account of patient history, symptoms, empirical findings on examination (e.g., blisters, pain locations), treatments applied and their effects, inferred diagnoses, and final outcome or discharge instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the case of Margaretta Lauwer: the report details onset at age, chronology of symptoms and relapses, treatments (demulcents, mercurial salivation, venesection, baths, clysters), observed reactions (vomiting of clysters with stones), inferred diagnosis (nephritis), and eventual clinical course and discharge.
